correctness.rationale: The frozen proof gives correct sharp bounds and eigenspaces, but the literal lower equality clause excludes the zero polynomial although the inequality is quantified over all f and both sides vanish at zero. The replacement gives both full equality spaces, including zero, and clarifies the dimensions in the optional exact enumeration. Torus rotations diagonalize the chamber Gram matrix in monomials; the probability-normalized moment α!/(d)_m and the |e_α|² tilt give Dirichlet(α+1). Gamma normalization cancels from the ordering, and conditioning on G1 gives the rational spectrum by expansion and gamma integration. Coupling integer shapes by additional independent exponentials strictly favors degree in the selected coordinate for the maximum and moves it into the rivals for the minimum. At fixed t>0, q_a/F_(a−1) is strictly increasing in a by the displayed reciprocal series, hence F_a/F_(a−1) is strictly decreasing. Comparing products of successive ratios proves F_a F_b>F_0 F_(a+b) for a,b>0, ensuring strict improvement when merging rival degree and establishing the lower equality space. The upper evaluation uses the gamma Laplace transform; exponential exchangeability divides the complement by k−1 for the lower value. The first nonconstant inclusion-exclusion term proves the fixed-k asymptotic, and Haar symmetry handles m=0. At (k,m)=(3,2) an independent direct integral gave the intermediate probabilities 47/108 and 7/54, distinct from 85/108 and 23/216 as required.
residual_risks: Finite exact enumeration in the frozen script is over length-k compositions (d=k); it is supplementary and does not alone establish endpoint comparisons in ambient dimensions d>k or all degrees. The analytic allocation argument handles all such dimensions.
